The owner sends it back

“Keep the failing request and the control result. Test a missing caption, check the data read, and show a regression check before asking for approval.”

Version 1 · investigation proposed.

The exact source, scope, observations, competing hypotheses and proposed work receive one digest.

Send back · instructions retained.

The first investigation remains readable. Its review reason stays attached to version 1; the previous digest cannot approve a revised plan.

Version 2 · evidence added.

A local agent submits its checks through the existing scoped connection. The owner compares both versions and decides on the new digest.

Approve or reject · work preserved.

Approval records the proposal decision. A separate authorised handoff must check the current target and source before execution. Rejection closes that proposal and keeps its evidence.

The private page uses the existing proposal store, workspace roles, source checks and review endpoints. A viewer cannot decide; an agent cannot approve itself; stale versions and revoked grants are refused.

What remains a separate check

Real failure detection, authorised recovery, configured owner email and PagerDuty each need their own recorded proof. This replay establishes none of those. The local availability lab already exercises a separate visibility failure and recovery; it is not a production responder.
